text:
maria: Draft PR up — updating the SDK migration guide around audit-log tenant semantics. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/492 (draft). Need SOC2-friendly wording for how tenant identifiers are logged and what counts as PII.
jon: ok, can you paste the current snippet here so i can eyeball?
maria: current sample in PR:
```json
{"tenant_id": "t-12345", "user_email": "alice@example.com", "action": "update"}
```
liam: For SOC2 language we should avoid 'anonymized' — legal prefers 'pseudonymized' when there's reversible mapping. Also call out that mapping tables are access-controlled.
zoe: Agreed. Also we should add a small migration example showing the SDK change (tenant_id -> tenant_hash) and a short python snippet. I can update the snippets.
maria: Proposed phrasing in PR: "Tenant identifiers are recorded in audit logs as pseudonymized tenant hashes; mappings to tenant metadata are maintained in a separate access-controlled store and are only accessible to authorized personnel for incident investigation." Thoughts?
jon: Nice. Maybe shorten "access-controlled store" -> "restricted mapping service"? keeps docs readable.
mia-legal: Quick review from Legal: prefer explicit phrase 'audited access' instead of just 'authorized personnel'. Suggest: "...accessible only to authorized personnel with audited access for security investigations."
liam: That reads better for SOC2 auditors. Also add a parenthetical about encryption-at-rest for audit exports.
ops-bot: Deploy preview for PR 492 available: https://deploy.previews.redwood/492 — build passed.
zoe: small technical nit — the SDK snippet still shows `tenant_id`. We'll change to `tenant_hash` and an inline note: "do not log raw tenant identifiers".
maria: updated PR with that change + retention example: "default retention: 90 days; configurable via export.retention_days" and a sample curl for export deletion.
jon: can you paste the updated SDK snippet?
maria: updated snippet:
```python
# client.audit.log_event(user_email=None, tenant_hash='sha256:...')
client.audit.log_event(tenant_hash=hashlib.sha256(b'tenant:acme').hexdigest(), action='update')
```
liam: tiny nit: show example of pseudonymization method in prose, not code: auditors like to see the algorithm named (e.g., SHA-256 with secret salt).
mia-legal: Approved with minor edit: include phrase 'salted hashing' and clarify access controls. Wording suggestion: "Tenant hashes are produced using a salted hashing process; mapping tables are restricted and access is logged and audited."
zoe: i'm running the link-checker for the API anchor references — found two broken anchors in the API reference (audit-exports section). i'll push a nav fix.
maria: thanks. @zoe can you also add a one-line changelog entry in migration notes under v2.1 about tenant->hash so customers notice?
zoe: added changelog entry and fixed two anchors. CI green.
jon: once legal signoff is in, i'll merge. any other blockers?
mia-legal: LGTM. :white_check_mark: Please keep the phrasing conservative as discussed.
maria: merging now. :shipit: Thanks all.
zoe: can we add a short FAQ blurb: "Why did we change tenant_id to tenant_hash?" and mention privacy + key rotation implications. i'll add after merge.
maria: added FAQ in follow-up commit. Closing thread.
jon: thanks everyone.
zoe: thanks!
